rulings.finding: Sustained. At the time of the audit, Tide of Life, Soulmend and Briar Wall each carried a two-rank Discipline prerequisite, which places them at the Adept tier, yet they printed their base Weak/Standard/Strong block on the Novice row 2/4/6, where ch08's budget table (Adept = 2 Disciplines = 6/9/12) and ch10's tier mandate ('a card bought at Adept tier starts at 6/9/12') require 6/9/12. The opening rung sat a full damage row under budget and each card's own Adept line merely restated the 6/9/12 the base should have carried, so the middle rung added no depth. The chapter contradicted itself: Restoration and Flesh Renewal hold the identical two-rank Life prerequisite and open at 6/9/12, and ch11's arcane two-rank cards (e.g. Brimstone Burst, 2 Fire) open on the middle row as well. This was a genuine off-budget deviation, not a rival card-template reading, and the three cards have since been re-rowed to 6/9/12.

Sustained. Ch21's glossary defines 'Resistance' as the typed-damage halving rule and ch22's reference sheet repeats that meaning, while ch12's divine cantrip of the same name instead grants a Boon on a Fortitude check (its Strong rung adding a flat -3 to certain typed damage, not halving), and ch20 overloads the word with a third sense ('Magic Resistance', 'Legendary Resistance'). 'Resistance' is the only word shared between the book's 81 glossary-defined terms and its 63 spell names, so this is not a tolerated naming pattern but a unique single-lookup failure: a reader who consults the term gets the halving rule and resolves the cantrip incorrectly, and the glossary carries no entry or pointer for the card's sense. The defect is real and the remedy is editorial: rename the cantrip, or add a disambiguating glossary line plus a see-also on the card.

Sustained as to the live layout defect: the chapter's cards are not atomic units and multiple cards straddle page boundaries in the built book. Inspecting the current 364-page PDF shows p181 ending inside the Virtue cantrip with its Standard rung overleaf on p182, a card cut between its Strong and Adept rungs across p184/p185, and a further split across p185/p186. Because a card body carries no grouping or keep-with-next construct, a rung run or a card is routinely severed at a page turn and must be bound with a keep that still permits splitting a card longer than one page. The companion sub-claim that the repo's orphan-heading checker is blinded by a markdown-only regex is STALE and is not sustained: commit c76ceb4 widened the harvest to Typst equals-prefixed headings, and the checker at HEAD now reports stranded headings book-wide. The ruling rests on the observable page splits alone, not on checker blindness.

rationale: I ruled each topic on the presented arguments cross-checked against the sources the brief permits. Topic 1 is the strongest: the audit-time revision of ch12 printed 2/4/6 base rows on three cards whose own Disciplines lines (2 Life, 2 Life, 2 Plants) fix them at the Adept tier, and ch08's budget table and ch10's explicit 'starts at 6/9/12' both bind that tier to the middle row; ch12's Restoration (2 Life) and Flesh Renewal (2 Life) plus ch11's Brimstone Burst (2 Fire) all open on 6/9/12, so the trio was an intra-chapter contradiction rather than a legitimate variant, and the repo's own disposition re-rowed them. Topic 2: the collision is real and uniquely severe because 'Resistance' is the single word in the book that is both a glossary-defined rule term and a spell title, the cantrip's actual effect (a Fortitude Boon, with a flat -3 clause) is not the halving rule the glossary and reference sheet fix, and the card offers no signal of the other sense; I sustained it as an editorial terminology defect with a low-cost remedy. Topic 3: the page-breaking is a live layout fact, confirmed by extracting the rendered pages, so rejecting the topic wholesale would be wrong; but I expressly declined to endorse the checker-blindness sub-claim, which the brief flags and the repo history confirms as repaired by c76ceb4, so the sustain rests only on the card splits. Nothing in the arguments changed my reading of the sources, and where the round-two findings corrected round-one counts (five of six splits, not six; 12 stranded at HEAD, not 15) I adopted the corrected figures.
